aspect: Roughly one in five blast injuries involves acute TBI
description: An estimated 20% of those with blast injuries suffer acute TBI, most cases mild - which is the category most likely to go unrecorded.
energy_note: Mild, in the sense that nobody wrote it down.

aspect: Symptoms persisting past fifteen years, with no direct head trauma
description: A documented case report describes blast-related TBI sustained with no loss of consciousness and no direct head impact, with chronic post-concussive symptoms persisting over fifteen years.
energy_note: Fifteen years of symptoms from an injury with no wound.

aspect: The symptom list is indistinguishable from a psychiatric one
description: Headache, tinnitus, dizziness, nausea, fatigue, hypersensitivity, irritability, memory deficits, depression. Referred to psychiatry, the neurological component goes untreated; referred to neurology, the psychological one does.
energy_note: Two specialties, each sure it is the other's patient.

aspect: The mechanism is degenerative, not static
description: Animal work indicates blast TBI produces auditory neurodegeneration, chronic vascular remodelling and blood-brain barrier degradation, associated with increased post-blast stroke and haemorrhage risk.
energy_note: An injury that continues working after the war.

aspect: SCENARIO - the man who is not lazy
description: He was thrown against a wall by pressure in 2014 and walked away. In 2026 he cannot hold a schedule, loses words mid-sentence and sleeps eleven hours. Three employers have concluded he does not want to work.
energy_note: Fired repeatedly for a brain injury nobody recorded.
